functional_requirements: Customer supporting document upload for claims
Claim officer request for additional information
Policy management (create, read, update, delete policies)
Policy holder management (create, read, update, delete policy holders)
Document management (upload, store, retrieve, verify documents)
Multi-level approval workflow configuration and execution
Comprehensive audit logging for claim activities
Notification sending for claim status changes
non_functional_requirements: Security (authentication, authorization, data encryption, data privacy)
Performance (efficient claim processing, responsive user interface)
Reliability (data integrity, accurate claim processing, dependable notifications)
Compliance (adherence to relevant insurance regulations and internal policies)
risks: Data security breach of sensitive customer, policy, and claim information.
Non-compliance with insurance industry regulations or data protection laws (e.g., GDPR, CCPA).
Incorrect claim decisions (e.g., approving fraudulent claims, rejecting valid claims) due to system errors or flawed verification processes.
Failure of notification delivery, leading to poor customer experience or missed service level agreements.
Performance bottlenecks during peak usage, impacting system efficiency and user experience.
Scalability limitations preventing the system from supporting future business growth.
Loss or corruption of uploaded supporting documents due to insecure or inadequate storage.
Incomplete or inaccurate audit logs, compromising regulatory compliance or internal investigations.
User authorization failures leading to unauthorized access to sensitive functionality or data.
Complex integration with existing core insurance systems or third-party services leading to project delays or data inconsistencies.
assumptions: Detailed policy coverage rules and claim adjudication criteria will be clearly documented and provided.
Existing policy data and policyholder information will be available in a structured format for migration or integration.
Specific formats, maximum file sizes, and verification rules for uploaded supporting documents will be defined.
Email is the primary channel for sending notifications unless other channels are explicitly requested.
All required external regulatory and internal compliance standards are known, documented, and will be provided.
The 'Administrator' role will primarily focus on system configuration, user account management, and master data related to policies and claim types.
The client will provide clear definitions, including data points and layouts, for all 'operational and claim-related reports'.
No immediate integration with external core insurance systems or payment gateways is required beyond fetching policy data initially.
questions: What specific types of insurance policies (e.g., auto, health, property, life) and corresponding claim types will the system need to support?
What are the detailed business rules and decision logic for claim adjudication and policy coverage verification for each policy and claim type?
What external systems (e.g., core insurance platform, payment gateways, fraud detection tools, CRM) require integration with this system, and what are the specific integration points?

Please define the exact requirements for 'multi-level approval workflows', including the number of levels, specific roles involved at each stage, and the approval logic (e.g., sequential, parallel, conditional).
What are the precise requirements for 'operational and claim-related reports', including specific metrics, data points, filters, frequency, and desired output formats (e.g., PDF, Excel, dashboards)?
What are the maximum file sizes and acceptable file formats for uploaded supporting documents? Are there any requirements for document OCR, content extraction, or AI-driven verification?
Beyond email, what other notification channels (e.g., SMS, in-app alerts, push notifications) should the system support for customers and internal users?

What specific functionalities are expected for the 'Administrator' role, particularly regarding system configuration, user management, and policy master data management, beyond policy/policyholder CRUD operations?

What are the anticipated peak and average user volumes (customers, claim officers, administrators) and transaction volumes (claims submitted, policies managed) in the short-term (1 year) and long-term (3-5 years)?
What specific regulatory compliance standards (e.g., HIPAA for health, PCI DSS for payments, local data privacy laws) must the system adhere to?
Are there any requirements for managing policy renewals, endorsements, cancellations, or premium adjustments within the 'policy management' module?
How should disputes or appeals related to claim rejections be handled and tracked within the system's workflow?
